Any tilt produces continuous gyroscopic precession: the lean direction rotates around the contact point and may damp toward vertical at high RPM or widen as RPM falls, but it never freezes at one lean angle or compass direction. Mechanical energy then decreases monotonically through friction and impacts: orbit speed and RPM decay, precession widens, the rim or base may scrape, and a fully stopped unsupported top falls onto its side.
